Chapter 10: Applying the Framework—Everyday Moral Challenges
Now, let’s bring everything we’ve talked about down to earth.
The real power of any moral framework doesn’t just live in abstract ideas—it shows up in the choices you make every day, in your relationships, and in those moments when you’re not quite sure what’s right.
So, how can these principles actually guide you through real-life situations?
Take promises, for example.
Maybe you’ve been tempted to break a promise because it feels easier or more convenient.
But before you do, try asking yourself—what if everyone did this?
If you couldn’t honestly wish for everyone to break promises whenever it suited them, that’s a pretty good sign you should keep yours.
It’s all about respecting the other person’s autonomy, even when it’s tough.
Then there’s the question of helping others.
Let’s say you’re deciding whether to lend a hand to someone in need.
Are you acting in a way that honors their dignity and freedom?
It’s not just about being nice—it’s about seeing and treating people as valuable in themselves.
Or think about your professional life.
Acting with honesty and integrity isn’t just about avoiding trouble or getting that gold star—it’s about doing what’s right because it’s right.
To make this practical, here are some tools you can use every day:
First, try the universalization test. Before you act, ask yourself, “Could I really want everyone to follow this rule?”
Next, do a respect check. Are you treating others as an end in themselves, not just as a means to your own goals?
And finally, give yourself an autonomy reminder. Are you choosing freely, guided by your own reason, or just going along with pressure or habit?
Here’s a metaphor to keep in mind: Living morally is a lot like tending a garden.
The principles you believe in? Those are your seeds.
But it’s your daily choices—what you say, what you do, how you treat people—that are the water and sunlight helping those principles grow.
Sure, you’ll make mistakes. Everyone does.
But with care and attention, a life built on integrity and respect really can flourish.
So, as you head into your day, remember: the framework isn’t just something to think about—it’s a way to show up in the world, one choice at a time.
